evidence: all ten registered FX images visually inspected
nominal: Bank supports explicitly named reciprocal quotes. Graphs and default e use foreign currency per domestic currency, U.S. dollar for FX. Increase means domestic appreciation only under this orientation.
real: epsilon=eP/P*. For physical baskets, (foreign currency/domestic currency)*(domestic currency/domestic basket)/(foreign currency/foreign basket) = foreign baskets/domestic basket. Index-based epsilon is normalized, not a literal basket exchange quantity.

models.coreFX: FX-01 through FX-08 and MACRO-56: gross currency demand from foreign goods/assets purchases, supply from domestic purchases abroad. Upward supply; equilibrium gross quantity is not automatically NX or NCO.
models.policyFX: FX-09/10 and MACRO-57: vertical supply=NCO determined in loanable funds, demand=NX; rate plotted as nominal foreign currency/USD. Hold domestic/foreign prices fixed to map to real exchange rate.
models.loanableFunds: Selected POL-H-003 explicitly has saving supply and I+NCO demand, equilibrated by domestic real interest rate.
models.trade: With NCO fixed, tariffs change FX demand/rate but not equilibrium NX.
models.shortRun: Monetary and AD items are conditional short-run channels; distinguish from fixed-NCO long-run trade adjustment.
